verdict.rationale: Stripe documents a seller-controlled allow model. Sellers pick which agents to sell through and only the seller can initiate an Order Connection Agreement (OCA), which authorizes data access. Either party can terminate an OCA at any time, so sellers can effectively allow or revoke specific agents. Nothing documents rate-limiting agent access to the catalog or checkout. Missing for 10: per-agent rate-limiting controls, explicit deny/block controls at the agent-platform level, and independent or hands-on corroboration (ACS is in private preview).

support.subject: As a merchant, I can rate-limit, allow, or deny specific agents and agent platforms accessing my catalog and checkout

citations.quote: Find the agent you want to sell through and review its terms
Only a seller can initiate an OCA request
After both parties confirm the OCA, it authorizes data access between your agent and the seller
Either party can terminate an OCA at any time.
